Getting started with CoDa Stereo

Source: vignettes/CoDaStereo.Rmd
CoDaStereo.Rmd

CoDa Stereo is a ‘shiny’ application for compositional data analysis (CoDA) of stereological, histomorphometric and blood-cell count data. Volume fractions from point counting, area percentages and differential cell counts carry only relative information: each part is meaningful only relative to the others. CoDa Stereo analyses these data with log-ratios (the Aitchison geometry) and does not apply standard statistics to raw percentages.

Launching the app 

library(CoDaStereo)
run_app()

Follow the sidebar from top to bottom. The guided tour (Tour button) walks through each step.

Workflow

  1. Data Upload. Load a CSV or Excel file and select the columns that form the composition (the parts). Non-numeric columns such as treatment or site become candidate grouping factors. A pre-flight check flags parts on an incompatible scale. Five examples are built in: a simulated liver dataset and the four case studies of the companion paper.

    When rows are fields of view nested within specimens (for example three fields per animal), tick Aggregate rows by specimen: fields of the same animal are not independent replicates. Point counts are summed; areas or proportions are averaged.

  2. Data Inspection. A three-state heatmap distinguishes observed values, zeros and missing values.

  3. Zero Handling. Log-ratios are undefined for zeros, so zeros are replaced before analysis. Use CZM for count zeros (point counting), and multRepl or lrEM for rounded zeros (values below detection). Missing values can be dropped or replaced by the column geometric mean.

  4. Compositional Analysis. Ternary diagrams (with optional amalgamation when there are more than three parts, and 95% confidence or predictive regions per group), the clr-biplot, the variation matrix, and the compositional centre and total variance per group. Open How to read this biplot for guidance on interpreting rays and links. Every figure can be exported as PDF, PNG, SVG or TIFF.

  5. Balances (SBP). The automatic sequential binary partition can be edited cell by cell. The CoDa dendrogram shows the mean and variance of each balance and its distribution per group; each balance can be tested between groups.

  6. Statistical Modeling. Permutational MANOVA on ilr coordinates (RRPP::lm.rrpp()) with factors, covariates and a block term, pairwise comparisons of means and dispersions, and residual diagnostics.

  7. Reproducibility. Download an R script that reproduces the analysis, a self-contained HTML report, or save the session to resume it later.

The interface is available in English, Portuguese and Spanish (EN / PT / ES in the header); a link can open the app directly in one language, e.g. ?lang=es.

When to include the total

By default only the composition is analysed, which discards the total. When parts are measured on an absolute scale (for example, compartment volumes obtained as volume fraction times Cavalieri organ volume, or cells per microlitre), the total can carry biological information. Choose Total (size) in the Statistical Modeling tab to analyse the log-total jointly with the ilr coordinates, or as a covariate to ask whether the composition changes with size. The sum of parts (Ts) is the default; the product total (Tp) is equivalent to analysing the log of each part (Pawlowsky-Glahn, Egozcue and Lovell 2015, doi:10.1177/1471082X14535526).

In point-counting stereology the total is usually fixed by design: the same number of grid points, fields or cells is counted for every specimen. That total carries no biological information and should not be included. The app warns when totals are almost constant.

Deployment

The repository root contains an app.R entry point and a manifest.json for deployment on Posit Connect Cloud.
